chosen: Write the interview-questions brief so a writer builds questions FROM the research question, with a worked before/after repair table. Briefs enable the writer; they do not replace their judgment.
rejected: Give the writer a fixed universal question list to copy into the article. One protocol fits all theses.

chosen: In a how-to brief, mark which parts need verify-before-drafting: Spradley question types confirmed in the actual source, ethics-committee wording quoted from the committee's own text. Never let a writer quote from memory.
rejected: It is a craft guide, not an academic paper — the writer can paraphrase the question types from what everyone knows.

chosen: When drafting a brief title, count the characters against the 60-char cap and verify the count programmatically; if the estimate is off, correct the estimate line to the ground truth.
rejected: The title looks about 55 characters — write the estimate in the brief and move on; nobody will check.

chosen: Keep the kanoon qualitative lane's internal-link map consistent across briefs: Brief D (analysis tool), Brief G (how many interviews), Brief L (how to write the questions), each promising bidirectional links. One lane, one map, no orphaned promises.
rejected: Each brief can link wherever looks relevant; the internal-link promises from older briefs are the writer's problem to reconcile.

chosen: In the interview-questions brief, explicitly forbid tricks the article could tempt: inventing a correct number of questions, implying homoglyph-style shortcuts for the مشابهت report, or presenting the protocol as committee-proof. Honest craft, no shortcuts.
rejected: Make the brief maximally conversion-friendly: promise the article will hand students a protocol that always passes and fixes their similarity percentage fast.

chosen: Qalam-check the brief twice: once on the Persian strings, once on the whole file — regular spaces everywhere, no U+200C anywhere, and any quoted user wording preserved verbatim.
rejected: Qalam-check the outline headings; the meta description and FAQ questions can be checked later by the writer.
